items.title: Phoebe Jacobs and Jackie Harris interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 21, 2006
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...some of them really know about Buddy Bolden, you know, and those guys in that era.

ctx.x: As some of the people I’ve talked to complain that some of the young people think that jazz history started with John Coltrane you know.

Well those kids don’t live in New Orleans obviously. You know if you were to ask young people about, well some of them really know about Buddy Bolden, you know, and those guys in that era. But in New Orleans if you were to ask some that maybe hadn’t been studying it they will tell you that Louis Armstrong was the first one. And that is the real unique thing about New Orleans is we know the history of the music.

It’s such a rich but sometimes confusing history racially with the Creole influence and all the nationalities there. Has that atmosphere, has a racial atmosphere let’s say pre-Katrina at least, what was it like?
